title: Chicken With Lemon Orzo In a Pot
description: From Nigella Lawson: “A family favorite, it's a simple one-pot dish that brings comfort and joy, and it is my pleasure to share that with you. It's not in the spirit of things to be utterly speciﬁc with this kind of cooking: If you're feeding small children, for example, you may not want to add the red pepper ﬂakes. Similarly, you may want to use just one lemon, rather than the two I like. It's also open to variation, owing to what's in your kitchen. I could go on, but there is no need to add complications. This is a simple recipe that brings deep contentment.”
ingredients: 3 big garlic cloves, chopped or minced or grated
2 medium or little peeled carrot pieces
2 medium leeks, sliced white/light green parts only
2 teaspoons flaky sea salt or kosher salt, or 1 tsp salt
1/3 cup finely chopped Italian parsley, plus more for serving
directions: Peel garlic cloves. Peel and cut carrots into three lengths across, and then into sticks (or, just use little peeled carrots).

Heat oil in a large heavy Dutch oven with a tightly fitting lid over high heat. Place chicken in hot oil skin side down and sear until skin is richly golden; 3 to 5 minutes. Take chicken out temporarily and put on plate.

Take Dutch oven off heat and finely grate in zest from lemons. Add garlic, dried tarragon, and leeks, followed by salt and red pepper flakes (if using). Squeeze in juice from your zested lemons and give a quick stir.
Pour in cold water — covering all but the very top of the chicken — and put Dutch oven back on high heat to bring to a boil.
Once it's bubbling, cover with lid and carefully transfer to oven. Cook chicken for 35 minutes, then check to make sure chicken is all but cooked through and carrots are soft.

Remove pot from oven and add orzo all around chicken, pushing it under liquid and stirring as best you can manage in the restricted space. Cover pot with lid and return to oven. Cook until orzo is soft and swollen, about 15 minutes.
Remove Dutch oven from oven and let stand, covered, for a few minutes before serving; orzo will continue to soak up broth as it stands.
While orzo finishes, chop parsley. Stir in ¼ cup, then sprinkle over a little more.
